newsitem.title: USA: Nasdaq shares crumble, blasted by tech stocks.
newsitem.headline: Nasdaq shares crumble, blasted by tech stocks.

text.p: Technology stocks clobbered the Nasdaq composite index down 25 points, the tenth largest one-day point drop.
Nasdaq stocks traded lower for most of the session, led by weakness in personal computer makers and networking stocks.

The downward spiral gained strength after the bond market slipped late in the day, traders said. Sell programs accelerated the decline, pushing the Nasdaq Composite Index down 1.84 percent to 1348 at the close. The Dow industrials lost 87 points, or 1.27 percent, to close unofficially 6747. The long-bond lost 19/32 to yield 6.75 percent.

"Mentally, it's still perceive as a big drop, but on a percentage basis, it's really not as significant as it was when the Dow was at 2700," said Brett Discher, vice president of equity trading at Dain Bosworth.

Technology stocks lost ground following Cisco Systems Inc second quarter earnings, which were released after the market closed Tuesday. Cisco shed 4-3/8 to 62-3/4 on fears of slowing growth. Intel Corp also crumbled 7-1/2 to 157-1/4 after some analysts downgraded the stock.
Traders said technology stocks could show further weakness at the opening, but recover throughout Thursday's session.
